visualizerParams.title: Code Refactor: Relink Pointers Instead of Copying Values
visualizerParams.problemDescription: The values are copied into a list and written back in reverse order. Reverse the list by changing the next pointers instead. The output must stay the same.
visualizerParams.initialCode:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next


head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3, Node(4))))
values = []
node = head
while node is not None:
    values.append(node.value)
    node = node.next
node = head
for value in reversed(values):
    node.value = value
    node = node.next
out = []
node = head
while node is not None:
    out.append(node.value)
    node = node.next
print(out)

solution.code:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next


def reverse(head):
    prev = None
    while head is not None:
        nxt = head.next
        head.next = prev
        prev = head
        head = nxt
    return prev


node = reverse(Node(1, Node(2, Node(3, Node(4)))))
out = []
while node is not None:
    out.append(node.value)
    node = node.next
print(out)
solution.explanation: Relinking uses three pointers and no extra memory, while the copy needs space proportional to the list length. It is also the answer interviewers expect.
